method: Three actually inspected ordinary pictures plus current standard PMTiles. No bespoke archival or survey research.

references.observed: Actually inspected the long warm-yellow and white south palace facade. Large paired upper windows with white pilasters and triangular window pediments sit above arched lower openings. A deep layered cornice and low green hipped roof lead to the raised central ornamental pavilion, green domed roof, gold lantern and slender finial. Plain original geometric trim will replace figurative emblems and inscriptions. The red Kremlin wall/tower and separate white/gold churches in the foreground/right are independent context.

Actually inspected the palace corner and side-facing elevation: warm-yellow walls, white trim, rounded lower windows and paired tall upper openings in two visible rows, narrow corner pilasters, triangular window pediments, continuous gray stone base, green hipped roof and raised roof-edge band. This photograph does not establish every rear roof or hidden facade.

Actually inspected oblique whole palace aerial. The principal southern yellow/white range has a large raised green domed central pavilion and connects to long side returns around an actual open courtyard. Lower green roofs and an ornate red-and-white, gold-domed historic group occupy the northern courtyard edge. Separate white/gold cathedrals and bell tower stand east across Cathedral Square; modern State Kremlin Palace stands beyond the northern group and remains native. A smaller attached gold-domed group at the southeast corner requires explicit scope reconciliation, rather than being silently dropped or merged with independent cathedrals.
